title: I've finally released my survival RPG on Android!
author: SuggestionFunny7236
selftext:
Hey everyone!  
I've been working on a game called Frontierfall, and it's finally live on Google Play! 😅  
It's a free survival RPG with expeditions, loot, bosses, companions and character progression.  
It's been a massive learning experience, and I'd love some honest feedback from anyone willing to give it a go!  
[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ironsignalgames.frontierfall](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ironsignalgames.frontierfall)  
**AI disclosure:** I've used generative AI extensively to help develop the game, including coding, content creation and development support.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body:
Hey u/SuggestionFunny7236, this falls under Rule 4. Sharing your game is okay here, free or paid, but you need to talk about how it was developed using AI, so the community has something to discuss. This post doesn't have enough on that yet.

To keep it up, edit your post or reply to this comment within an hour with some details on your dev process, like:

- which AI tools you used, and what for
- how they fit into your workflow
- problems you hit and how you dealt with them

"Made with AI", a list of tools or a ChatGPT bullet list won't cut it. If nothing's added by then, this post may be removed.

If you think we got this wrong, [message the mods](https://www.reddit.com/message/compose?to=/r/aigamedev).

replies.author: SuggestionFunny7236
replies.body:
Hey, thanks for pointing this out! Happy to explain a bit more.

I'm a solo developer building Frontierfall in Godot, and ChatGPT has played a pretty big part in helping me get it off the ground.

I've used AI extensively for coding, debugging, planning gameplay systems, working through UI designs and helping develop game content and artwork.

My workflow has basically been coming up with ideas, working with AI to implement them, then loading everything into Godot on my Android phone to test it myself.

And it's definitely not been plain sailing! I've had crashes, broken menus, performance issues, Google Play integration problems and plenty of things that worked in theory but completely failed when tested.

A lot of the development has been going back and forth, testing things, recording bugs, making changes and testing again. Sometimes fixing one thing breaks three others!

AI has made it possible for me to tackle a project much bigger than I could have managed on my own, but there's still been a huge amount of trial and error involved.

I'm still learning and improving the game, which is partly why I'm sharing it here. I'd love to hear how other people are approaching AI-assisted game development too.

Hopefully that gives a bit more insight into the process!
